correctness.rationale: At a deterministic horizon, reversing the iid copying arrows traces each site back either to a correct source or to an initially incorrect ordinary site. Consensus is absorbing, so T≤t is exactly the event of no unanchored lineage after t reversed arrows. At j distinct unanchored sites, selecting one of the j sites and copying one of the z+j−1 source/other occupied sites drops the count by one with probability p_j. Positions may otherwise move, but the count kernel does not depend on them. The strong Markov property gives independent geometric waiting times with support starting at 1, including the case m=1. Partial fractions of (1−E[s^T])/(1−s) give the survival coefficients; the j=1 coefficient is the telescoping product m(z+1)/n. All rates are strictly ordered and less than 1. For fixed z, scaling each fixed waiting time by n² gives its exponential limit and the uniform remainder bound is the convergent tail sum of 1/[j(j+z−1)]. This proves the limit, with finite mean and nonzero variance. Splitting off E_1 and using an exponential moment for the remaining sum above rate z proves the limiting tail, whose product coefficient tends to z+1. Euler's sinh product evaluates the one-source transform; shared copying preserves sitewise order and proves worst-case dominance. A separately written exact-rational finite check passed 770 forward/geometric CDF and 770 spectral-survival comparisons over 55 populations 2≤n≤11, 1≤z<n and 0≤t≤13, plus 55 leading-coefficient comparisons. Replay procedure: propagate the count distribution from j=m using up and down probabilities j(m−j)/n² and j(n−j)/n²; independently propagate a pure-death chain with decrements p_j, and compare both CDFs and the displayed survival sum at each tick. The tridiagonal comparison in the frozen verify.py follows the same finite scope; neither finite test proves the limit.

evidence: Corujo's Theorem 1.3 gives the eigenvalues of the Moran generator as linear combinations of mutation eigenvalues minus (p/N)j(j−1). For the one-way boundary use reverse rate epsilon>0, whereby the two-type generator is irreducible and the nonzero mutation eigenvalue is −(z+epsilon); let epsilon decrease to zero. Continuity of the finite characteristic polynomial gives the eigenvalues −j(j+z−1) with p=N, including j=0.

Fill's Theorem 1.2 applies to the consecutive correct-count chain started at its lower endpoint, with absorption at its upper endpoint and positive internal birth/death probabilities. Its non-unit eigenvalues are positive, 1−j(j+z−1)/n², so the theorem immediately gives independent geometric summands.
Jenkins–Spanò §2.1 defines the classical entrance-from-infinity pure-death chain with rates j(j+theta−1)/2 and §2.2 gives its exact probabilities, crediting Griffiths and Tavaré.

Its transient spectrum is a direct boundary specialization of Corujo's explicit neutral Moran spectrum, and Fill's exact birth–death passage-time theorem gives the claimed independent geometric sum from those eigenvalues. The fixed-source limit follows directly by scaling these factors with a summable mean bound and is the classical absorption law of the coalescent with mutation after deterministic time rescaling. value.rationale: The absorption distribution is a meaningful invariant and the graphical proof is concise. The frozen contribution, however, consists of an equivalent specialization of a known finite spectrum and passage law, followed by direct moment, residue, and fixed-rate scaling computations into a known limit law. The graphical proof uses the standard arrow construction with sources treated as absorbing ancestors and does not establish a separate new structural claim on other graphs or protocols. A convenient derivation of the exact specialization does not on its own establish scientific value at the required bar.
